name: MERIT
aliases: D-MannosE to prevent Recurrent urinary tract InfecTions
question: Does daily D-mannose taken for 6 months reduce the proportion of women with recurrent urinary tract infection who have a further medically attended infection?

design.population: 598 women aged 18 or older (mean age 58) with at least 2 UTIs in the preceding 6 months or 3 in 12 months, recruited from 99 primary care centers in England and Wales.
design.description: Multicenter, double-blind, placebo-controlled superiority randomized trial
design.locator: PDF p1 (abstract), p2 (Participants, Randomization and Masking), p5 Table 1

verdictNote: Not significant; the 95% CI for relative risk (0.80 to 1.05) excluded the 50% reduction the patient panel required.
takeaway: In a double-blind trial of 598 women with recurrent UTI in UK primary care, daily D-mannose 2 g for 6 months did not reduce medically attended, clinically suspected UTI versus placebo (51.0% versus 55.7%; risk difference −5 points, 95% CI −13 to 3).

reports.label: Primary report (JAMA Intern Med)
reports.citation: Hayward G, Mort S, Hay AD, et al. "d-Mannose for Prevention of Recurrent Urinary Tract Infection Among Women: A Randomized Clinical Trial." *JAMA Intern Med.* 2024;184(6):619-628. doi:10.1001/jamainternmed.2024.0264
reports.followUp: 6 months per participant; recruitment March 28, 2019 to January 31, 2020

results.measure: Proportion with at least 1 further episode of clinically suspected UTI for which ambulatory care was contacted within 6 months; unadjusted risk difference, D-mannose minus placebo, in percentage points
results.note: Adjusted relative risk 0.92 (95% CI 0.80 to 1.05; P=0.22) from a log-Poisson mixed-effects model with practice as a random effect. Primary outcome data were available for 294/303 and 289/295 randomized women; the trial was powered to detect a 50% relative reduction. Per-protocol, imputation and preplanned subgroup analyses gave similar estimates.
results.locator: PDF p1 (abstract), p3 (Statistical Analysis), p4 (Primary Outcome), p7 Table 2

results.measure: Number of clinically suspected UTIs over 6 months; adjusted incidence rate ratio, D-mannose versus placebo
results.note: Incidence rate ratio from a log-Poisson mixed-effects model; 9 and 6 women had missing data. The sample size was set to be adequate for this outcome.

results.endpoint: Time to next consultation with clinically suspected UTI
results.measure: Adjusted hazard ratio, D-mannose versus placebo (mixed-effects Cox model); incidence per 1000 days at risk
results.note: Time at risk 36 263 versus 33 337 days; 2 participants with a consultation on the day of randomization were excluded.

results.endpoint: Days of moderately bad or worse UTI symptoms
results.measure: Symptom-diary days over 6 months; adjusted median difference, D-mannose minus placebo (quantile regression)
results.note: Diary data were missing for 63 and 66 women. Weekly symptom burden score: adjusted median difference 0.00 (95% CI -0.37 to 0.37; P>0.99).

results.measure: Number of microbiologically proven UTIs over 6 months; adjusted incidence rate ratio, D-mannose versus placebo
results.note: Microbiological data were missing for 54 and 51 women; urine samples were those sent by clinicians for routine care.

results.measure: Number of prescribed antibiotic courses for UTI over 6 months; adjusted incidence rate ratio, D-mannose versus placebo
results.note: Defined daily dose, adjusted mean difference -0.10 (95% CI -0.23 to 0.02; P=0.11).

results.endpoint: Days of prescribed antibiotics for UTI
results.measure: Days of antibiotics prescribed for UTI over 6 months; adjusted median difference, D-mannose minus placebo (quantile regression)
results.note: The report attributes the difference to a small number of women with very high antibiotic consumption (maximum 161 days in the D-mannose group, 66 days in the placebo group).

results.endpoint: Days of prescribed antibiotics for UTI
results.measure: Post hoc analysis excluding 12 women more than 3 SDs from the mean; mean days (SD); adjusted median difference, D-mannose minus placebo
results.note: Post hoc sensitivity analysis (eTable 7 of the report's supplement, which was not read).

results.measure: Women with resistant uropathogens cultured during an episode of infection; relative risk, D-mannose versus placebo
Women admitted to hospital for UTI during 6 months; relative risk, D-mannose versus placebo

harms.label: Serious adverse events (events, excluding hospitalizations for elective procedures)
harms.note: 28 events in total, among 303 and 295 randomized women; counts are events, not participants. None was judged related to the intervention.

harms.label: Adverse effects given as the reason for discontinuing the study product
harms.note: Listed under discontinued medication in the flow diagram. An adverse event that prevented compliance with trial procedures was recorded in a further 1 and 2 women.

delivery.label: Regimen

values.exp: About 2 g of D-mannose powder as one daily scoop for 6 months
values.ctl: A similar daily scoop of fructose powder

delivery.note: White powders of similar sweet taste in identical bottles. Packs were sent every 2 months and both products were continued during symptoms and while taking antibiotics. Both products were purchased from Tiofarma.

delivery.label: Women who initiated the study product
delivery.note: Percentages calculated from the flow diagram counts.

delivery.label: Reported adherence
delivery.value: More than two-thirds of women reported taking the study product at least 3 days a week for 15 weeks.
delivery.note: Adherence was similar in the 2 arms; the report states that the per-protocol analyses restricted to women reporting good adherence gave similar effects.

delivery.label: Women who believed at 6 months that they had received D-mannose
Recruitment
delivery.value: 7591 women invited, 830 responded, 232 excluded or not randomized (139 eligible but not randomized), 598 randomized.
delivery.note: Recruited from 99 primary care centers between March 28, 2019 and January 31, 2020.

delivery.label: Withdrawals
delivery.note: The Results text and the flow diagram give different counts of withdrawn, discontinued or lost women.
